The earlier decision relied on the assumption that exploring commits in topological order ensures all reachable commits are considered before processing a specific commit. However, the new evidence shows that using generation numbers instead of commit dates can lead to incorrect behavior if a commit reachable from an older version (like v4.8) can also reach the target commit (B), thus changing its applicability. This new evidence suggests that the earlier result holds true when generation numbers do not introduce such incorrect behaviors.
